design.title: Patchwork surveys: random rectangles of every training view are replaced by the SAME ground from another survey (or, sometimes, by unrelated ground), so a place must be recognised from whatever survives local change
design.eli5: We teach the model Berlin from three aerial photographs taken in different years, then test it on a fourth it has never seen. Between photographs, little pieces of the city change: trees gain leaves, shadows move, a car park fills up, a building site grows. So while training, we cut random rectangles out of each picture and fill them with the same spot as it looked in another year's photograph, or occasionally with a piece of somewhere else entirely. The model can no longer rely on one or two memorable details; it has to recognise the place from everything around them, which is what it must do when the new photograph has changed a few details of its own.
design.hypothesis: Champion exp 20 (0.0777) on held-out truedop_2024: usable 93.0%, false fix 0.75% (3 frames), abstain 6.25% (25 frames); the three training photographs score 100% usable / 0% false at the same held-out viewpoints, so the whole remaining score is the survey gap, and it is mostly abstention. Every survey-invariance mechanism this era has kept or tried acts on the WHOLE frame at once: photometric/blur nuisance (exp 4), MixStyle feature statistics (exp 14), weight averaging (exp 20), JS consistency of beliefs across surveys (exp 23, reverted), and the pretrained trunks (exps 12-19). None of them touches what actually differs LOCALLY between two surveys of the same ground: one block's trees are in leaf in one capture and bare in another, a courtyard is in shadow in one and lit in the next, a car park is full or empty, a construction site has moved on. A GAP-pooled place descriptor trained on three captures can lean on whichever few distinctive patches all three happen to agree on; when one of those patches differs in 2024, the descriptor moves off its prototype, the committee members' mass spreads, and the frame abstains (or, rarely, lands confidently elsewhere). The four captures are registered to one grid within 1 px, so the training set already contains the exact local substitutions a fourth survey makes: the same pixels of ground as photographed by another survey. Pasting rectangles of another training survey into a view, at the same ground position and heading, manufactures a new 'survey' per view whose season, shadow and contents vary REGION BY REGION, a combinatorial family the three whole photographs never show. A smaller share of rectangles filled with unrelated ground (another position in the batch) stands in for change that no training survey contains (new buildings, demolition). The training signal is then: the label stays put while any ~10-40% of the frame changes, so the descriptor must spread its evidence across the frame's stable structure instead of a few fingerprint patches. Builds on exp 6 (pixel blending of whole surveys, reverted on the from-scratch trunk of that time) by making the mixing spatial and local rather than a global alpha blend, and on exp 14's insight that cross-survey mixing helps, carried from feature statistics to content. Plateau note: exps 21-26 were four reverts of training-procedure and trunk-weight variations; this changes a stage never questioned in the era, the CONTENT of the training views (only their photometry, sharpness and heading have ever been randomised).
